doc: Two friendly rifle squads 20 m apart are ordered onto the same point 35 m east (sw-txnj.12, GDD 02 §2.14 Separation and coherency). Separation pushes units of different squads apart to their size-class distance (troopers are medium: 0.6 m), so squads that share ground interleave instead of stacking. Squad footprints (sw-txnj.13) now give two squads ordered onto one point footprint points apart, so base and attack_move both end a footprint apart and are checked for the 0.6 m gap only. Variant arrive_on_squad: one squad already standing on the point when the other arrives (no footprint, since it holds rather than moves), which keeps the interleave check. The far post is an unarmed, stationary dummy that only keeps player 2 in the battle.

arrive_on_squad.doc: North already holds the point; south moves onto it.

probes.doc: While they arrive, a pair may overlap for a tick: a push is capped at the unit's speed (walk per tick when it stands), so two units stepping onto one slot take two ticks to part (0.32 m at worst here).
Settled, no unit of one squad is closer than 0.6 m (medium) to a unit of the other, on any tick of turn 3 (they arrive late in turn 2).

They end interleaved on the point, not just kept apart: the nearest pair is within 2 m. Only where one squad holds the point: two squads ordered onto one point now get footprint points apart (sw-txnj.13), so the base and attack_move variants end a footprint apart and this probe doesn't apply to them.
Spacing within one squad (separation never pushes a squad's own units); reported only.
